subsystems.name: Material supply
subsystems.role: stores and delivers the food inks that will be printed.

subsystems.name: Printhead
subsystems.role: deposits droplets or continuous lines of each ingredient.

subsystems.name: Motion system
subsystems.role: moves the printhead and build plate in three axes.

subsystems.name: Control and software
subsystems.role: turns a recipe into a print path and coordinates the hardware.

subsystems.name: Post-processing
subsystems.role: sets, cooks or assembles the printed shape into a finished dish.

subsystems.name: Ingredient preparation
subsystems.role: turns raw ingredients into printable inks with the right flow properties.

buildSteps.title: Design the recipe and print path
buildSteps.detail: Define the target food's structure, texture and nutrition, then convert it into a 3D model and a map of which material goes where.

buildSteps.title: Formulate printable inks
buildSteps.detail: Blend proteins, fats and carbohydrates with thickeners or gelling agents until each ink has the viscosity and particle size the nozzle can handle.

buildSteps.title: Load and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Fill the cartridges, purge air from the lines, and calibrate nozzle alignment and the volume deposited per droplet or line.

buildSteps.title: Print layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The printer deposits droplets or lines of different inks according to the model, building the food from the bottom up.

buildSteps.title: Apply in-situ processing
buildSteps.detail: Heat, cool or UV light sets each layer as it is printed, or a gelling agent is co-deposited to lock the structure.

buildSteps.title: Post-process
buildSteps.detail: The printed item is cooked, baked or assembled with other components to finish it.

buildSteps.title: Quality control
buildSteps.detail: Inspect shape, texture and, where possible, nutrition, then adjust printing parameters for the next run.

prerequisites.why: inkjet and extrusion of food pastes are demonstrated, but not at the molecular precision the tile implies.
the rheology of printable food inks is an active research field, with many ingredients still unprintable.
some machines handle two or three pastes, but combining many ingredients without cross-contamination is hard.
laser cooking and hot-air finishing are researched, but reliable, fast setting of printed layers is not solved.
building food from individual molecules is not possible today; current printers work with pastes and gels.

pathway.milestone: single-material printers for chocolate, pancake batter, pasta and puréed foods
pathway.unlocks: custom shapes and textures for niche diets.

pathway.milestone: multi-material printers that combine proteins, fats and carbohydrates with in-line cooking
closed-loop printers with sensors that adjust composition in real time
pathway.unlocks: precise control of flavour, texture and nutrient content.

pathway.milestone: molecular-level assembly from basic chemical building blocks
pathway.unlocks: arbitrary food synthesis, but this remains speculative.
